entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Bank Leumi (National Bank of Israel) is Israel's second-largest bank, founded in 1902 in Jaffa as the Anglo-Palestine Company, a subsidiary of the Jewish Colonial Trust (itself established by Theodor Herzl in 1899 to finance Zionist colonization). Bank Leumi predates Bank Hapoalim by 19 years and Israel by 46 years, making it the financial institution most directly connected to the Herzlian Zionist project.

The bank's evolution parallels Jewish statehood: from the Anglo-Palestine Company (1902) under British colonial law, renamed the Anglo-Palestine Bank (1930), then Bank Leumi (1950) after Israel's establishment. Herzl himself helped establish the Jewish Colonial Trust, which capitalized the Anglo-Palestine Company, making Bank Leumi the direct institutional descendent of political Zionism's first financial instrument.

Bank Leumi's 2014 US settlement — paying $400 million for helping American clients evade taxes through secret Israeli accounts — followed the pattern of Swiss bank UBS (2009), HSBC (2012), and Bank Hapoalim (2019), as US authorities systematically dismantled banking secrecy globally. The bank serves 1.9 million customers in Israel, with international offices in London, New York, and Zurich serving the Jewish diaspora. Israel's banking system is unusual in being dominated by two banks (Hapoalim and Leumi) with combined market share exceeding 65%.
